title: Comparison of the determinants of two exact two-periodic complexes joined by a morphism vanishing on kernel and cokernel
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of exact (2, 1)-periodic complexes of finite length modules over a local ring whose maps induce zero on both the kernel K and the cokernel Q, the lemma asserts that det_kappa(M, phi, psi) equals det_kappa(alpha_0^{-1} o alpha_1) times det_kappa(M', phi', psi'), where the two isomorphisms Q -> K come from the boundary maps of the two short exact sequences of complexes displayed in the statement (statement lines 17107-17139). The proof is a long and explicit computation rather than a formal manipulation: the author first identifies the two boundary maps concretely as composites through the intermediate quotients I_{phi'}/alpha(I_phi) and I_{psi'}/alpha(I_psi) (proof lines 17149-17210), then does a length bookkeeping with k = length(K), a = length(I_phi) and b = length(I_psi) showing length(M) = length(M') = a + b while length(N) = a + b - k and length(Q) = k (proof lines 17163-17173), and finally chooses admissible sequences generating K, I_phi and I_psi together with preimages under phi and psi, compares the two determinants through the characterisation by admissible sequences, and tracks the scalar obtained (proof lines 17212 onward). The author explicitly notes that an alternative enormous commutative diagram exists and chooses the admissible-sequence route instead, which is why the argument is a delicate bookkeeping computation. Coordinating the boundary maps with the admissible sequences and their preimages is not a routine exercise, so the claim is H3.
